A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Family Matters study and M2A framework. Their main text, equations, 11 tables, 21 figures, and Appendix A.1–A.11 support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification experiments, adaptation and ablation results, and CarlaTTA semantic-segmentation experiments, including results in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and appendix segmentation evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same masking families, random selection, masking schedule, consistency-plus-entropy objective, and per-batch adaptation procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10-C, CIFAR-100-C, ImageNet-C, MRSFFIA-C, and CarlaTTA, with the same classification, segmentation, and streaming scenarios. The new black-box adaptation citation does not introduce an evaluated task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding main-text and appendix experiments. For example, Table 1 retains REM, Continual-MAE, SPA, DPCore, and PAID. The newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Splits, backbones, metrics, budgets, and reset procedures are unchanged, including ten-seen/five-unseen domain transfer (Table 2), ten-pass lifelong adaptation (Table 3), and MRSFFIA-C severity resets (Table 7).

E4.justification: The mask-sampling comparisons, hyperparameter and loss ablations, alternative update strategies, small-batch tests, spectral and feature analyses, sample trajectories, and selection-heuristic comparisons are retained. Appendix reflow adds no analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seeds 1, 2, and 3 and mean/standard-deviation reporting in Section 4.2. Uncertainty entries and statistical reporting practices, including those in Tables 1, 3, and 11, are unchanged.

E6.justification: All 11 tables match, and figure results and qualitative findings are retained. For example, Table 1's M2A patch mean errors remain 8.9%, 19.8%, and 37.4% on CIFAR-10-C, CIFAR-100-C, and ImageNet-C, respectively.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(24) and Appendix A.3's conceptual formalization are unchanged, including retained energy, spatial coherence, spectral overlap, and heuristic stability conditions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about masking-family-dependent stability and architecture–task alignment. The qualification that system-level heuristic comparisons do not isolate selection strategy is also retained.

C2.justification: The structural-preservation interpretation and limitations concerning unequal information removal, causal isolation, random selection, and architecture/task dependence remain unchanged in Section 4.7 and Appendices A.3, A.10, and A.11.

D1.justification: Optimizer settings, learning rates, batch sizes, parameter updates, MI200 hardware, and CarlaTTA/MRSFFIA-C processing details are unchanged. No code/data availability or access instructions change.

R1.justification: v4 adds Maharana et al. (2026), Continual test-time adaptation: A comprehensive survey, and Zhang et al. (2026), Adapting in the dark: Efficient and stable test-time adaptation for black-box models. These background citations expand the references without substantively changing research positioning.

P1.justification: v4 replaces numerous em dashes with commas and revises author/contact text, including adding Habib Ullah's email. The narrative, section order, and substantive paragraph content remain intact.

P2.justification: The author/affiliation block is reformatted, and references and appendix material reflow. Figure 6 moves from page 22 to 23, and Figures 20–21 shift by one page. Figure and table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 adds limited bibliographic context and reformats the front matter, while appendix reflow is less compact, including a nearly empty page 34. Methods, evidence, interpretations, and limitations remain unchanged. These editorial differences do not produce a meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
